comments.author: Dannii
comments.content:
Thanks for the write-up!

Once software gets stable there's no shame in letting it sit for a while, especially if it's open source and you're willing to take contributions. I've lost a lot of interest for Parchment - I had big plans for adding a library to it, but I honestly can't see myself finishing it anymore. But as long as it doesn't get crippled by bugs the lack of additions doesn't harm it! Sounds like Quest is in the same kind of position.

comments.author: Pertex
comments.content: I am very unhappy with this :,-( . It sounds like the slow but final end of Quest. Is it time to search a new IF project where we can find a new home?

comments.author: Dannii
comments.content: I thought you might also like to know that Hitchhikers is getting played almost 3k times a month via Parchment, and your referrals for it are 16% of all plays on Parchment! Your referrals for all games are over 37% of Parchment's plays.

comments.author: Neil
comments.content:
I read about your Squiffy development, interesting that yout thought a 'simpler' system seems more appropriate for your needs when actually writing an adventure.
If you take a more detailed look at Twine (and Twee), you'll probably see that it is pretty much the same thing as Squiffy. Keeping it simple to actually write, but making the system open enough so that you can get directly at the HTML, CSS and JavaScript if you really need to.
